text:
ana (design): dropped a couple of quick prototypes for the compact timeline + inspector. want feedback on keyboard behavior and the undo toast wording.
thomas (product): saw the images, thanks. main goal: make rollbacks discoverable but not scary. wording is the hard part.
ana (design): small correction: my name is ana, not nana :sweat_smile:
thomas (product): oops, fixed 😅
nana (design): also fixed the comps — new thread below.
rachael (a11y): quick reads: 1) keyboard entry into inspector must preserve source focus 2) toast undo needs ARIA role and clear context 3) slider needs 4.5:1 contrast when focused.
kai (eng): under the hood we can route keyboard events to the timeline container while it has active focus. to avoid clash with slash search we can only listen when inspector-open=true.
nana (design): thinking out loud: flow should be: focus on active variant card -> Enter opens inspector -> left/right cycles snapshots -> U opens undo draft? maybe U is too magic.
rachael (a11y): prefer standard keys: Enter open, Arrow keys navigate, Space or Enter to open details, and Esc to close. avoid adding new single-letter shortcuts unless global docs are updated.
nana (design): noted. for the undo flow, I sketched a toast: "Changed active variant to v12 — Undo" with a 10s visible CTA. Is that okay?
thomas (product): wording: "Changed active variant" is a little bland. customers asked for "Reverted traffic to snapshot v12" before. Which is clearer?
rachael (a11y): both okay, but the aria-live announcement should be explicit: "Reverted traffic to snapshot v12. Actions: Undo" and the Undo control should receive focus if keyboard used to perform the action.
kai (eng): impl note: making the toast focusable and moving focus there is doable, but it interrupts screen readers if we yank focus too often. we should only focus the toast when the action originated from keyboard.
nana (design): good point. we can conditionally focus based on input modality. also add an "Open version history" link in the toast for more safety.
oliver (research): if we're going to focus the toast, make sure there is a clear tabstop order so keyboard users can continue to relevant controls. Also can we get a quick usability test with 3 keyboard-only participants? 15m each.
thomas (product): let's run a quick lab next Tue. oliver can you recruit?
oliver (research): on it.
rachael (a11y): copy nit: avoid "revert" vs "rollback" ambiguity. propose using "Revert to snapshot v12" in UI and in aria: "Reverted to snapshot v12; traffic now directed to this snapshot. You can undo from the banner or in Version History."
nana (design): thanks — that reads better. I'll use "Revert" as the label on the toast and keep the primary CTA in inspector as "Rollback" to align with engineering docs. slightly different but okay?
kai (eng): mixing terms could confuse users. prefer consistent label across flows. if we choose "Revert" I can map it to the same API call.
thomas (product): let's align on "Revert" across the board. less charged.
rachael (a11y): agreed. also include a short description for screen readers attached via aria-describedby: "This action sets the active variant and will route traffic according to allocation. To undo, open Version History or press Undo in the banner."
nana (design): ui detail: compact timeline collapses to a chevron + count. when inspector opened from compact mode, show a "Full timeline" button to expose the full scrubber. keyboard users should be able to tab to it.
kai (eng): performance note: live traffic updates may re-render timeline and move focus. we should freeze UI diffs while inspector is open and queue updates. debounce window of 2s should be fine.
rachael (a11y): freezing is ok if there is a visible notice: "Live updates paused while inspector open" and an sr-only live region for critical failure messages.
nana (design): added that to comps. also increased hit targets for slider ticks and added Shift+Arrow to nudge by 1% and Arrow to nudge by 5%.
thomas (product): are we comfortable exposing 1% nudges? could be dangerous in high-traffic environments. maybe limit to dev mode or require confirmation for >20% changes.
kai (eng): can add a client-side confirmation modal if the change delta exceeds a threshold. UX will show a small confirmation rather than blocking every nudge.
rachael (a11y): confirmation modal must be accessible: focus trap, labelled by heading, and first actionable button is primary.
nana (design): I'll mock the confirmation modal copy: "You27re about to increase allocation from 5% to 25%. Confirm to apply." buttons: "Confirm" and "Cancel".
thomas (product): tweak Confirm to "Apply change". cancel remains.
rachael (a11y): also ensure the modal explains rollback path: "You can revert this in Version History."
nana (design): action items: 1) ana update comps (compact + toast + modal) 2) rachael draft aria-describedby and toast aria examples 3) kai implement focus/keyboard scoping & debounce 4) oliver recruit 3 keyboard-only participants.
thomas (product): timeline: can we get engineering estimate? kai?
kai (eng): rough: scoping & prototype 2d, modal + toast accessibility 1d, QA + polish 1d. call it 4 dev days.
thomas (product): ok. schedule research session after prototype ready.
